gaps.sentence: ___ she felt nervous, she delivered a flawless speech.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' introduces a full clause and is stronger than although.

gaps.sentence: ___ his salary, he earns royalties from three textbooks.
gaps.explanation: 'In addition to + noun' adds one source of income to another.

gaps.sentence: He talks ___ he owned the place.
gaps.explanation: 'As if/though + past' describes behaviour contrary to fact (he doesn't own it).

gaps.sentence: Far from resenting the changes, the staff welcomed them; ___, productivity rose.
gaps.explanation: Rising productivity is an additional point in the same direction: moreover.

gaps.sentence: Sales fell sharply last quarter; ___, the board cut the dividend.
gaps.explanation: The fall in sales caused the cut: as a result marks the consequence.

gaps.sentence: She is not only a gifted violinist ___ a composer of some note.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only A but also B' joins the two parallel noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: The drug trial was halted ___ an irregularity in the data.
gaps.explanation: 'Owing to' + noun phrase gives the reason in formal register.

gaps.sentence: ___ the price, the location is absolutely perfect.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from the price' = the only negative in an otherwise positive description.
